01-one-shot.py: 5 biology problems (3 errors, 1 warning, 1 note).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 10 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at
least)
   line 49:  p300.mix(3, 10, well_dst)
   At line 49 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 10 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this
   line did it 21 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong
   amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator
   passes the move. Wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 3.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [7f3918c3a88f]

2. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A2 in slot 3: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 49:  p300.mix(3, 10, well_dst)
   At line 49 the p300_single_gen2 draws 10 ul from well A2 in slot 3 with its tip 1 mm
   above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 25 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well
   Plate 200 µL Flat reaches only 0.79 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air
   (this line did it 21 times; 210 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does
   not follow the liquid. These are mixing strokes: the tip stirs air, and the well is not
   mixed. Source wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix lower, with `well.bottom(0.5)`, so the tip is in the liquid. This well needs
   about 35 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [2728a08a365c]

3. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 10 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at
least)
   line 58:  p300.mix(3, 10, well_dst)
   At line 58 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 10 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this
   line did it 21 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong
   amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator
   passes the move. Wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 3.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [393cf94869c8]

4. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: Mixing too weak to stir 7 wells: 3 × 10 ul in 50 ul
   line 58:  p300.mix(3, 10, well_dst)
   At line 58 the tip mixes wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 3 with 3 strokes of
   10 ul in a well holding 50 ul (this line did it 7 times). 3 strokes of 10 ul move 0.6 of
   the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of strokes to mix (the mixing work).
   Integra draws over 80% of the well five times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty
   gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated, and in a
   dilution series every later step inherits the error.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (40 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 40,
   well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [72fc0eebb826]

5. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No blank on a dilution series: 8 wells of bsa
   line 35:  p300.dispense(50, plate["A1"])
   At line 35 the robot starts a dilution series of bsa in NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat
   (slot 3): 8 wells at 8 concentrations, each level about 2 times weaker than the one
   before. No well on this plate holds water with no sample, so there is no blank: the curve
   has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic cannot be told
   from the lowest point. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 3.
   Fix: Add a well of water alone, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [8f4ea6c80ca8]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
